summary: Scanned iac-demo (1 Terraform module, 1 Kubernetes manifest, 1 Dockerfile) with trivy config 0.76.2 using the embedded checks, offline. 32 raw hits reduce to 2 exposures (SSH open to the internet, a privileged container that mounts the host filesystem) and 4 hygiene findings. The missing S3 public access block is a lead: the bucket has no public ACL or policy in this repository. Not covered: checkov was not run, and no Terraform plan was evaluated.

findings.title: Security group 'bastion' allows SSH from any address
findings.description: aws_security_group.bastion has an ingress rule for TCP 22 with cidr_blocks 0.0.0.0/0. Any host on the internet can reach the SSH service of every instance in this group, which exposes it to password guessing and to any SSH pre-authentication flaw.
findings.remediation: Set cidr_blocks to the administration network (for example ["10.0.0.0/8"]) or remove the rule and use a session manager instead of direct SSH.

findings.title: Deployment 'collector' runs a privileged container with the host root filesystem mounted
findings.description: The container sets securityContext.privileged: true and mounts hostPath / at /host. Code execution in this container is code execution on the node: the process can read and write every file of the host, including kubelet credentials. Three checks report this one cause.

proof.poc: jq '.Results[].Misconfigurations[]? | select(.ID=="KSV-0017" or .ID=="KSV-0121" or .ID=="KSV-0023") | {ID, Title, CauseMetadata}' evidence/artifacts/trivy-config.json

findings.remediation: Set securityContext.privileged: false, drop the hostPath volume, and mount only the directory the collector reads (read-only). Add allowPrivilegeEscalation: false and capabilities.drop: [ALL].

findings.title: Dockerfile runs as root from a mutable base tag
findings.description: The image has no USER instruction, so the application runs as root, and it builds FROM debian:latest, so two builds of the same commit can ship different base images. Neither is reachable on its own; both make a compromise of the application worse.
findings.remediation: Pin the base image to a version tag and digest, add a non-root user (RUN useradd -r app, then USER app).

findings.title: Hygiene: deployment misses pod security hardening
findings.description: Grouped hygiene hits with no direct attack path: no CPU or memory requests and limits, no read-only root filesystem, no seccomp profile, default pod security context and other pod-security-standard gaps on the collector deployment.

proof.poc: jq -r '.Results[] | select(.Target=="k8s/deployment.yaml") | .Misconfigurations[] | select(.ID != "KSV-0017" and .ID != "KSV-0023" and .ID != "KSV-0121" and .ID != "KSV-0125") | [.ID, .Severity, .Title] | @tsv' evidence/artifacts/trivy-config.json

findings.remediation: Add resources.requests and resources.limits, readOnlyRootFilesystem: true, seccompProfile.type: RuntimeDefault and runAsNonRoot: true at the pod or container security context.

findings.title: Hygiene: Dockerfile has no HEALTHCHECK and installs recommended packages
findings.description: The image builds without a HEALTHCHECK instruction and apt installs pull recommended packages, which grows the attack surface. Both are operational hygiene, no direct attack path.
findings.remediation: Add a HEALTHCHECK that matches the service and pass --no-install-recommends to apt-get install.

findings.title: Hygiene: bucket misses logging, versioning and customer-managed encryption
findings.description: The logs bucket has no access logging, no versioning and uses default S3-managed keys rather than a customer-managed KMS key. None of these open an attack path on their own; they weaken forensics, recovery and key control.
findings.remediation: Enable access logging and versioning on the bucket and set a customer-managed KMS key in aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration.

hypotheses.title: S3 bucket 'logs' has no public access block (AWS-0086, AWS-0087, AWS-0091, AWS-0093, AWS-0094)
hypotheses.rationale: The repository defines no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block for the bucket, but it also defines no public ACL or bucket policy. New buckets are private by default and the account may enforce a public access block. Nothing here proves the bucket is public.
hypotheses.next_step: Check the account-level S3 Block Public Access setting, or add an aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource with all four flags set to true.

hypotheses.title: Image pulled from a registry trivy does not know (KSV-0125)
hypotheses.rationale: registry.example.test is not in the scanner's list of trusted registries. Whether it is trusted is an organisation decision the repository does not record.
hypotheses.next_step: Compare with the organisation's registry allow-list or the cluster's admission policy.
